task_instance: Plan and synthesize a user research study on why new signups to a fictional project-management app ('TaskFlow') drop off during onboarding: produce a research plan, a semi-structured interview guide, a set of 6 sample interview note transcripts, a synthesis report (affinity-mapped themes + impact/effort prioritized recommendations), and a highlight reel of key quotes.
evidence: Created 5 markdown files in the work directory: research_plan.md (objectives, research questions, method rationale, participant criteria, timeline, deliverables, success criteria), interview_guide.md (5-part structure: warm-up/context/deep dive/reaction/wrap-up with probes, following the skill's stated Interview Guide Structure), interview_notes/P1_notes.md through implicit P1-P6 sections (6 realistic synthetic interview transcripts covering a mix of novice and experienced PM-tool users), synthesis_report.md (6 affinity-mapped themes derived from the notes, an impact/effort prioritization table per the skill's Analysis Framework, 5 prioritized recommendations, and answers to the original research questions), and highlight_reel.md (8 key quotes tied to specific themes/participants). Verified by reading synthesis_report.md back and cross-checking that every theme and quote traces to specific lines in the interview notes file. All deliverables listed in the skill's 'Deliverables' section (research plan, interview guide, synthesis report, highlight reel) were produced using only text file writes -- no code execution, shell commands, or binary files were needed, since the skill's core work (planning, question design, thematic synthesis, prioritization) is entirely a text-reasoning task achievable with Read/Write alone.
